metadata.baseline_vs_method: Ban-free forecasts of where the named modal ban lands: SUBTRACT (token vetoes of the default's distinctive n-gram, our method) and LADDER (generic pushes) vs the ASSOCIATE (free-form association) and PROXIMITY (AST edit distance) baselines, plus a UNIFORM reference; all scored by mean log score under one frozen smoothing.

metadata.selection:
The mini file keeps ONE dataset of the artifact's method_out.json, `modal_ban_samples`, cut from 1,200 to 100
examples: 10 tasks x 5 templates (W1-W5) x 2 samples.  R3 and T14 are left out to stay within the 100-example cap
(both fail the gate in the full run and have no disagreeing forecasts, so they never enter the C1 contest). Inside each (task, template) cell the 2 samples are allocated to labels by largest remainder of 2 x (the cell's
label share); ties go to the label most under-represented in the task's running allocation relative to its
full-run share; within a label the lowest sample index is taken.  The examples are written in allocation order, so
the first k examples of a cell are the best k-sample summary of it (the notebook's N_PER_CELL knob).
`--per-cell 20 --tasks all` writes the same format with all 1,200 ban samples (the full-scale input of the notebook).

  undefined (scored uniform, flagged) if no round has >= 20, or if D keeps >= 0.5 of attempts in every round

rule), FRLP_FP8 (exp11 baseline FRLP mass over survivors with mass >= 0.01 and Kish ESS >= 5, renormalised).
DISAGREEING = among the four primary families with a defined top-1 (>= 2 defined), the top-1s are not all equal.
